## Missouri's Hardest Golf Courses 

The state of Missouri is home to more than 300 golf courses, both public and private. These courses vary widely in difficulty, with some displaying wide differences between their own tee boxes. There are lots of great golf courses in the state, but some are particularly challenging. This article covers the 10 hardest golf courses in Missouri, based on the USGA Course Ratings. The USGA Course Rating is a measure of the difficulty of a golf course for a scratch golfer, and it takes into account factors such as length and hazards such as water, bunkers, and trees. Length is a primary driver of course rating. The courses listed here are ranked by their "Rating to Par," which is the difference between the course rating and its par. Ties were broken by the course's "Bogey Rating to Par". Special layouts on courses designed to push the course beyond its layouts are not included in this list (think Bellerive Country Club's 2018 PGA Championship layout). If you really think you want a challenge, this list is for you, but if we're being honest, only the top 0.01% of golfers should play from these lengths.

## 1. Fox Run Golf Club (Eureka, MO)

Fox Run Golf Club is a par 72 course located in Eureka, Missouri, about 40 minutes southwest of St. Louis. The course has a rating of 77.3 from the black tees, implying even a scratch golfer would be expected to shoot 5 to 6 strokes over par. The course is known for its extreme length, measuring 7496 yards, which is the longest regular layout in the state. Unfortunately, the course is not open to the public, so it's much more difficult to get the opportunity to get beaten up by this course.

## 2. Oakwood Country Club (Kansas City, MO)

One of Kansas City's premier country clubs checks in as the second most difficult course in Missouri with a course rating of 76.9 from the black tees. The course has length, but is actually the shortest par 72 course on the list. Tight, tree-lined fairways and strategic bunkering and lakes make the course a true challenge. The course also boasts the highest bogey rating in the state, meaning that it brutalizes decent golfers even more than it does extremely good ones. 

## 3. Bellerive Country Club (Creve Coeur, MO)

Bellerive Country Club is one of the most famous golf courses in Missouri, due largely to its exposure hosting premier professional tournaments. The course that hosted the 1965 U.S. Open and the 1992 and 2018 PGA Championships plays 7460 yards on a normal day from the tips and boasts a 76.3 course rating. When players such as Bryson DeChambeau and Phil Mickelson shoot over par on the course, it doesn't bode too well for the average golfer who thinks he's a pro. 

## 4. The Golf Club at Creekmoor (Raytown, MO)

The name of the back tees at the Golf Club at Creekmoor is "The Beast," and it lives up to its name. The course has a rating of 76.3 on the beast layout. If you go to play you must sustain your focus for a whole round as the back nine plays markedly more difficult than the front. The good news about this course is that it is the first course on the list that is open to the public (although it will run you up about $100). 

## 5. Branson Hills Golf Club (Branson, MO)

The southern tourist town claims the fifth most difficult course in Missouri, and the first not in or near a major population center. Branson Hills has a course rating of 76 from the gold tees, but fortunately for anyone not quite as good as they think they are, has the lowest slope rating of the top 10 courses (at 132). The course is known for elevation changes and dramatic views. It is open to the public, but can cost as much as $175 to play at peak times. 

## 6. Blue Hills Country Club (Kansas City, MO)

Chalk up another point for difficult country clubs in Kansas City. Blue Hills Country Club is another par 72 course and features a course rating of 75.8 from the "7.4" tees. The tee naming comes from the length of the course, which is approximately (with some generous rounding) 7.4 thousand yards. The Robert Dunning designed course is a true test and plays host to the Korn Ferry Tour's AdventHealth Championship. 

## 7. Boone Valley Golf Club (Augusta, MO)

Boone Valley Golf Club is the only par 71 course that cracks the top 10, with a course rating of 74.7. The back nine boasts a ridiculous slope rating of 155, the highest slope possible (which means if you're not scratch don't even try these tees). The course is located in Augusta, Missouri, about 50 minutes west of St. Louis. Surrounded by tree-covered hills, the course is easy on the eyes and hard on the scorecard. The course has previously played host to a variety of Senior and Junior championships.

## 8. Meadowbrook Country Club (Ballwin, MO)

Another course on the west side of the St. Louis metro area, Meadowbrook Country Club is a par 72 course with a course rating of 75.7 from the black tees. The club prides itself on its course conditions and the course branding. Meadowbrook has all of the factors that make a course difficult.

## 9. Dalhousie Golf Club (Cape Girardeau, MO)

The bootheel's beast at Dalhousie Golf Club is a par 72 course with a course rating of 75.7. The Nicklaus Design course has hosted a variety of lower level championships and in 2015, hosted the USGA Women's Team Championship. The course takes the natural geography of the land turns it into something beautifully challenging.

## 10. Aberdeen Golf Club (Eureka, MO) 

Not to be outdone by its neighbor Fox Run, Aberdeen Golf Club is a par 72 course with a course rating of 75.7. It is the 7th longest course in Missouri playing 7332 yards. The good news for people who think they're better than they actually are is that this course is not as difficult as many of the others on the list for bogey golfers (ranking 31st on Bogey Rating to par). This difference is due largely to the links style of the course.
